original_question: Is classicality the only source of commutativity for virtual long knots, in the sense that whenever long knots K and K' satisfy K#K' isotopic to K'#K, there must exist a virtual long knot L, classical long knots Q and Q', and non-negative integers m and n such that K = L^m#Q and K' = L^n#Q'?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 20, "Non-Commutativity and Long Knots." It is motivated by the Section 2.2 discussion of long virtual knots, where the paper explains that connected sum is well defined for long knots and need not be commutative in the virtual setting. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation: it uses the commuting hypothesis K#K' isotopic to K'#K, asks for a decomposition through a common long virtual factor L together with classical long knots Q and Q', and correctly keeps m,n as non-negative integers. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, specify that K and K' are long virtual knots and that isotopy is taken in the long-knot category; the paper's earlier discussion identifies long knots with 1-1 tangles. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Define # as the ordered connected sum for long knots; the paper relies on the fact that connected sum is well defined for long knots, unlike the compact virtual case. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Define L^m explicitly as the connected sum of m copies of L; the paper states this immediately after Problem 20. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

For faithfulness to the paper's intent, include the motivating premise that every classical long knot commutes with every long knot, and the question asks whether all commuting pairs arise only from that phenomenon in the stated factorized way. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

If one wants the m,n≥0 clause to be completely explicit, the usual convention for the 0-fold connected sum should be stated; the paper leaves that convention implicit while allowing non-negative m,n. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Let K and K' be long virtual knots, with # denoting the ordered connected sum in the long-knot category. If K#K' is isotopic to K'#K as long knots, must there exist a long virtual knot L, classical long knots Q and Q', and integers m,n ≥ 0 such that K = L^m#Q and K' = L^n#Q', where L^m denotes the connected sum of m copies of L? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Is the fact that classical long knots commute with every long knot the only source of commutativity for long virtual knots? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 7, Problem 20 rather than a neighboring problem. Section 2.2 develops the long-knot context: long knots are treated as 1-1 tangles, connected sum is well defined for them, and in the virtual setting it is not generally commutative. Section 7 then states Problem 20 by asking exactly whether a commuting pair K,K' must factor as powers of a common long virtual knot multiplied by classical long knots. Your draft preserves both the hypothesis and the conclusion almost verbatim; only a few contextual definitions and implicit conventions need to be made explicit for a completely stand-alone formulation. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
